sections.title: 31-37 THE SAME ANGELS WHO GAVE GOOD NEWS TO IBRAHIM ANNIHILATED THE NATION OF HOMOSEXUALS

translation.text: Abraham said, ‘What is your errand, messengers?’
They replied, “We have actually been sent to a wicked people,

commentary.text: That is, to the people of the Prophet Lut (PBUH). The description of a “wicked people” was enough in view of the gravity of their crimes.

Also see: Surah Al-Araf, Ayats 80-84, Surah Hud, Ayats 74-83;  Surah Al-Hijr, Ayats 58-79; Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayats 74-75; Surah Ash-Shuara, Ayats 160-175; Surah An-Naml, Ayats 54-58; Surah As-Saaffat, Ayats 133-137.

marked by your Lord for the transgressors.

commentary.text: Each transgressor had a clay stone marked for him.

translation.text: And We have left a sign there ˹as a lesson˺ for those who fear the painful punishment.

commentary.text: “A sign..” refers to the Dead Sea, southern part of which still presents the signs of a great disaster. The archaeologists have expressed the opinion that the principal cities of the people of Lut were probably sunk underground, and the waters of the Dead Sea spread over them.

The area to the south of the sea still abounds in the ruins and the underground stocks of sulfur, resin, tar and natural gas found in this area lead one to believe that Hell must have been let loose at this place at some time by the eruption of lava and the play of lightning.

Lesson: Don’t continue sinning under some false pretense of guise of justifying your sins. Pharon was fooled by his power and position. People of Lut continued to sin not thinking of the consequences and even today people commit zina and justify it.

sections.title: 38-46 THERE IS A LESSON IN THE STORIES OF FIR'ON, A'D, THAMUD AND PEOPLE OF NUH

intro.text: Stories of Musa, Ad, Thamud, and Nuh are being mentioned as past nations that denied and therefore destroyed. Take a lesson!!! These are not fables of the past but reminders and examples not to follow.
DON’T REPEAT THE MISTAKES OF THE PAST.

sections.title: 47-60 ALLAH, WHO BUILT THE HEAVENS AND SPREAD OUT THE EARTH, HAS ASSIGNED PROPHET MUHAMMAD TO BE A WARNER FOR MANKIND

translation.text: We built the universe with ˹great˺ might, and We are certainly expanding ˹it˺.

commentary.text: After presenting historical arguments for the Hereafter, that is corrupt nations were ultimately destroyed, now arguments from the universe are being presented in relation to Tauhid.
Proofs of Allah's Oneness abound in the Creation of the Heavens and the Earth.

translation.text: And We created pairs of all things so perhaps you would be mindful.

commentary.text: Everything in the world has been created on the principle of the pairs. Certain things are complementary and matching to certain others, and their combination brings into being countless new forms and combinations.
The creation of the whole universe on the principle of the pairs testifies to the necessity of the Hereafter.

When everything in the world has a partner and nothing becomes productive without combining with its partner, how can the life of the world be without a match and partner? Its match and partner necessarily is the Hereafter, without which this world would be absolutely fruitless.

translation.text: So ˹proclaim, O Prophet˺: “Flee to Allah! I am truly sent by Him with a clear warning to you.

commentary.text: RACE TOWARDS ALLAH SWT and Seek shelter and guidance only from Him. (Before it is too late).
Creation is weak and needly. Don’t fill a void through alcohol, relationships, work etc. Rather turn towards Allah SWT.

translation.text: And do not set up another god with Allah. I am truly sent by Him with a clear warning to you.”

commentary.text: DO NOT COMMIT SHIRK!! Do not set up partners with Allah SWT.

translation.text: Similarly, no messenger came to those before them without being told: “A magician or a madman!”

commentary.text: That is, this has not happened for the first time that the people are calling the Messenger sent by Allah SWT a sorcerer and a madman when they heard the news of the Hereafter and the invitation to the Oneness of Allah from him.

translation.text: So ˹now˺ turn away from them ˹O Prophet˺, for you will not be blamed.
But ˹continue to˺ remind. For certainly reminders benefit the believers.

commentary.text: In this Ayat a method of the preaching/dawa of religion has been taught which should be well understood. When a preacher of the truth has presented his message clearly before a person with rational arguments and has also removed doubts, objections and answered arguments, then he becomes relieved of his duty of making the truth plain. Even after this if the other person persists in his disbelief and creed, the responsibility for it does not lie on the preacher of the truth.
The preacher, in fact, has done his duty; if the other man is not convinced, leave him alone.

translation.text: I did not create jinn and humans except to worship Me.

commentary.text: THE PURPOSE OF OUR EXISTENCE IS MENTIONED HERE: Allah SWT created both the jinn and humans for the sole purpose of worshiping Him. This is the core purpose of their creation. Worship with love and submission to Allah SWT. Allah SWT needs nothing from us rather we need Allah SWT.
Lesson: Unlike the rest of creation which worships Allah SWT all the time, we have the freedom to choose. So choose wisely and align your life with the core reason we were created.

translation.text: I seek no provision from them, nor do I need them to feed Me.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is eternal that is He never needed anything before or after. He is not dependent on human worship for His power, status, or existence. He does not need support, offerings, or service to remain God. Worship is not for His benefit, but for ours, because we were created with the need to submit to Him. False gods depend on their followers to survive, to be protected, funded, and upheld. Allah SWT alone needs nothing, gives everything, and remains supreme whether people worship Him or not.

29-49 MISSION OF THE PROPHET AND THE RESPONSE TO THE DISBELIEVERS' ARGUMENTS

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This Surah too was revealed in the same stage of the Holy Prophet's life at Makkah in which the Surah Adh-Dhariyat (The Winds) was revealed.

front_matter.label: Subject Matter and Topics
front_matter.text:
The subject matter of its first section (1-28) is the Hereafter. As arguments for its possibility, necessity and occurrence had already been given in Surah Adh-Dhariyat, these have not been repeated here. However, swearing an oath by some realities and signs which testify to the Hereafter, it has been stated most emphatically that it will surely come to pass, and none has the power to prevent its occurrence.
Vivid description of Heaven and hell and what leads on to these destinations.

sections.title: 1-28 DENIERS OF TRUTH WILL BE PUT IN THE FIRE OF HELL AND REWARD FOR THE RIGHTEOUS WILL BE PARADISE IN WHICH THEY WILL SHOW GRATITUDE FOR ALLAH'S GRACIOUSNESS

translation.text: By Mount Ṭûr!

commentary.text: By the Tur, Allah SWT swears by His creation. At-Tur is the mount that has trees, like the mount where Allah SWT spoke to Musa (PBUH).  A mount that does not have trees is called Jabal, not Tur.
Ayat 2,3,4,5, and 6 Allah SWT takes oaths to establish what is being said below.

translation.text: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will come to pass

commentary.text: The conclusion or subject of the vow/oath is that THE DOJ IS A CERTAINTY!   Allah SWT’s torment will surely strike the disbelievers.
FYI – Throughout the Quran Allah SWT taking an oath indicates or shows the importance of what is being mentioned next.

translation.text: Then woe on that Day to the deniers—

commentary.text: Woe to them on that Day because of the torment, punishment and affliction that Allah SWT will direct at them.

translation.text: those who amuse themselves with falsehood!

commentary.text: During this lifetime they mocked and ridiculed the news of Resurrection, Hereafter, Heaven and Hell and instead of considering it seriously they are disputing it only for fun and amusement. Their discussions of the Hereafter are not meant to understand the reality, but only to amuse themselves, and they do not at all realize the fate for which they are destined.
These people spent their time on earth in meaningless endeavors and engaged in useless conversation and play.
LESSON: OUR TIME IN THIS WORLD IS VERY PRECIOUS AND FOR A PURPOSE! Excess talk or overindulgence should be avoided as it makes us heedless. We forget right from wrong.
Lesson: Beware and stay far away from those who make religion a subject of mockery and jest.

translation.text: ˹It is˺ the Day they will be fiercely shoved into the Fire of Hell.

commentary.text: The Day when they will be violently driven and shoved, to the fire of Hell, with a horrible, forceful pushing.

translation.text: ˹They will be told,˺ “This is the Fire which you used to deny”.

commentary.text: The angels of punishment who are the guards of hell will say these words to them, while admonishing and chastising them.

translation.text: As for those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith, We will elevate their descendants to their rank, never discounting anything ˹of the reward˺ of their deeds. Every person will reap only what they sowed.

commentary.text: IMAN + GOOD DEED = SUCCESS

In Heven each person is given their rank according to their deeds. Those who believe will be joined with their families. Allah SWT makes it clear that there will be no demotion only promotion. Family unity is essential with Allah SWT.
If parents’ level is higher than the children, then they will be elevated and vice versa. None will be lowered and reduced in rank

In this world our soul is locked and then in the next it will finally be free – but with the correct deeds. 

As for those of the children of a believer, who might have died even before reaching maturity, there cannot be any question of belief or disbelief, obedience or disobedience, for they will be admitted to Paradise automatically and will be lodged along with their parents to be a comfort of the eyes for them.

translation.text: They will turn to one another inquisitively.
They will say: “When we were living before among our kinsfolk we lived in constant fear (of Allah’s displeasure).

commentary.text: Conversation in Heaven between the dwellers of Paradise who will say to each other, that, “in the life of world when we were with our families, we were afraid of our Lord and fearful of His torment and punishment.” That is they lived a life a of constant alternes and caution. Even in the safely, security and comfort of their homes they were fearful of displeasing Allah SWT careful to fulfill their obligations (towards Allah and humans.)
Lesson: This is what brings people to Heaven.

translation.text: Then Allah graced us with His favour and saved us from the chastisement of the scorching wind.

commentary.text: Indeed, we used to call upon Him ˹alone˺ before. He is truly the Most Kind, Most Merciful.”
Allah SWT has granted us a favor and saved us from what we feared – Hell. Paradise is a HUGE FAVOR/BLESSING FROM ALLAH. Nothing we do will ever be good enough for us to enter Heaven.

translation.text: Indeed, we used to call upon Him ˹alone˺ before. He is truly the Most Kind, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: TAUHID. In this worldly life we used to invoke Allah SWT with submission and humility, and He accepted our invocation and gave us what we wished.
DID NOT COMMIT SHIRK.

sections.title: 29-49 MISSION OF THE PROPHET AND THE RESPONSE TO THE DISBELIEVERS' ARGUMENTS

translation.text: So ˹continue to˺ remind ˹all, O Prophet˺. For you, by the grace of your Lord, are not a fortune-teller or a madman.

commentary.text: After depicting a scene of the Hereafter, the address now turns to the disbelievers of Makkah and the stubbornness with which they resisted the message of the Prophet (PBUH).

This Ayat though apparently addressed to the Prophet (PBUH) is meant for the disbelievers through him. They would taunt the Prophet (PBUH) by saying that he was a sorcerer, or that he was a poet, or that he was a madman, or that he fabricated those strange things himself and presented them as Revelations from Allah SWT only to impress the people.
But Prophet (PBUH) is told to continue reminding people about Allah SWT because you never know when someone might accept.

translation.text: Do their minds prompt them to say such things, or are they a people immersed in transgression

commentary.text: In these two sentences, the opponents’ entire propaganda has been exposed and explained. The reasoning briefly is this: These Qaraish chiefs and elders pose as very wise people but then how can one and the same man be a poet and a madman and a sorcerer at the same time? If he is mad, he can then neither be a sorcerer nor a poet. If he is a sorcerer, he cannot be a poet, and if he is a poet, he cannot be a sorcerer, for the language and diction and themes of poetry are quite different from the language and themes of sorcery.

Therefore, it is evident that these contradictory things are being said against the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) not based on intellect and reason but only due to obduracy and stubbornness, and the big chiefs of the nation blinded by their prejudice and enmity are leveling absurd charges which no serious person can regard as worthy of any attention.

translation.text: Let them then produce something like it, if what they say is true!

commentary.text:
Not only is the Quran not the word of Muhammad (PBUH) but the truth is that it is not human at all; it is beyond the power of man to compose and produce it. 

(1) The Quran is the highest and most perfect model of the literature of the language in which it was revealed. No word and no sentence in the entire Book is sub-standard. Whatever theme has been presented in it, has been presented in the most appropriate words and in the most suitable style. 

(2) This is the one single Book in the world, which has so extensively and so universally influenced mankind’s thoughts, morals, civilization and way of life as has no precedent in history.

(3) The theme that this Book discusses is the most extensive theme which comprehends the whole universe, from eternity to eternity. It tells us who the Creator and Controller and Disposer of this universe is, what are His attributes, what are His powers, and what is that essence and basis on which He has established this entire system of the world.

It specifies man’s position and his place which he cannot change. It tells what the right and correct way of thought and action for man in view of this place and position is, which corresponds to the reality, and what are the wrong ways which clash with the reality.

It does not merely point to the right way but presents a plan of the complete system of life which contains a detailed and systematic code concerning beliefs, morals, purification of self, worship, social life, civilization, economy, politics, justice, law and every other aspect of human life.
Furthermore, it also tells in full detail what are the results of following this right way and of adopting the wrong ways in this world and what consequences of this will appear in the next world.

(4) This Book was not composed and written all at once and presented before the world, but a reformatory movement was started with some basic and initial instructions and then for 23 years as the movement passed through different stages of its development its parts were presented sometimes as lengthy discourses and sometimes as brief sentences, as the conditions and requirements of the occasion demanded.
Allah’s revelations in different conditions, are wholly devoid of human feelings. At no place can even an acute observer and critic point out the play of human feelings in them.

Although there are several other aspects also of the Quran's being a miracle, if a man ponders over these few aspects only, he will realize that the Quran’s being a miracle is far more evident today than it was at the time when it was revealed and, if Allah so wills, it will go on becoming more and more evident and manifest as time passes till the Day of Resurrection.

translation.text: Or were they created by nothing, or are they ˹their own˺ creators?

commentary.text: Allah SWT asks them, were they created without a maker or did they create themselves?

Ayat 36 till 44 Allah SWT asks disbelievers many other questions to make them understand, including Who created the Heavens and Earth? Who controls everything? Do you have any proof that Allah is not your creator? Does the Prophet (PBUH) ask you for compensation when conveying the message? Is any human controlling the universe?

translation.text: (So obstinate are they that) even if they were to see some fragments of the sky falling down they would still say: “It is only a mass of cloud.”

commentary.text: Despite all the questions posed by Allah SWT (above) that should provoke reflection the disbelievers continue to stubbornly and obstinately deny and deny. Allah SWT says even if reality is right in front of them they will deny.

translation.text: So leave them until they face their Day in which they will be struck dead

commentary.text: Allah SWT repeatedly told the Prophet (PBUH) esp in Makki Surah’s to leave those who are obstinate in their beliefs. They will face or meet their Day, in which they will sink into a fainting. (on the Day of Resurrection).

Lesson: To stubbornly deny is something that will lead to Hell. Remember that we all have times when we have low Iman but to be prideful and deny again and again is a sure-fire way to Hell. Excuse the pun.

translation.text: Also, the wrongdoers will certainly have another torment before that ˹Day˺, but most of them do not know.

commentary.text: Allah SWT sends smaller worldly punishments before the greater punishment of the Hereafter as a warning, not for revenge. These hardships are meant to shake people out of ignorance, remind them of divine authority, and give them a chance to repent. But most people don’t understand the message. When the crisis passes, they return to the same behavior, like a camel that gets tied and released without knowing why. The signs were there. The lesson was offered. The response was denial.
Lesson: Calamities aren’t random. They’re mercy in disguise.

translation.text: So be patient with your Lord’s decree, for you are truly under Our ˹watchful˺ Eyes. And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise.

commentary.text: Allah SWT repeatedly told the Prophet (PBUH) esp. in Makki Surah’s to leave those who are obstinate in their beliefs. O Prophet (PBUH) be patient over Allah SWT’s commands.
Allah SWT says, ‘You are in My sight and under My protection’.
Do tashbeeh and remember Allah SWT when we wake up, after salah or when we leave a gathering.
Lesson: It is soo comforting to know that we are not alone and that Allah SWT is watching and protecting not only His Prophets but all of us – in sha Allah. Ameen.
DUA FOR FIVE OCCASIONS:
After a gathering of zikr. This will be like a seal.
After a gathering that was a waste of time. This will be like a charity or kafara.
After wuzu. This will be a reward.
After salah. (Prophet (PBUH) did this.
After the recitation of the Quran. (Prophet (PBUH) did this.

translation.text: And glorify Him during part of the night and at the fading of the stars.

commentary.text: Night prayers and after each prayer glorify your Raab. Do tasbeeh and zikr during this time.
Lesson: Do Tasbeeh Fatima after each prayer. Say a dua when you wake up at night and do night prayers (voluntary) and Tahajud.
Prophet (PBUH) is encouraged to busy himself with worship, specifically salah and tasbeeh, when he is troubled or upset.
Similarly, we must do the same.
FYI – Surah ends with mention of stars and the next Surah is Surah Najam or The Star.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Sarah derives its name from the very first word.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Surah was revealed in the Ramadan of 5th year of Prophethood. This is the first Surah in which an Ayat required the performance of a prostration. This is the first Surah of the Quran, which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) had publicly recited before an assembly of the Quraish in which both the believers and the disbelievers were present. At the end, when he recited the Ayat requiring prostration, the whole assembly fell in prostration with him, and even those chiefs of the polytheists who were in the forefront of the opposition to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) could not resist falling in prostration.
In Rajab of the 5th year of Prophethood, a small group of Companions emigrated to Abyssinia. During Ramadan of the same year news spread that when the Holy Prophet (PBUH) recited Surah An-Najm publicly in the assembly of the Quraish, the whole assembly, including the disbelievers, fell in prostration. When the emigrants to Abyssinia heard this news, they formed the impression that the disbelievers of Makkah had become Muslims.
Thereupon, some of them returned to Makkah in Shawwal of the 5th year of Prophethood, only to learn that the news was wrong and the conflict between Islam and disbelief was raging as furiously as before. Consequently, the second emigration to Abyssinia took place, in which many more people left Makkah.

front_matter.label: Subject Matter and Topics
front_matter.text:
Three topics have been presented in their successive order:
Firstly, disbelievers are told that the religion that you are following is based on mere conjecture and invented ideas. You have set up a few goddesses like Lat, Manat and Uzza as your deities, whereas they have no share whatever in divinity. The reason for this is that you are heedless of the Hereafter. Only this world is your goal. Therefore, you have neither any desire for the knowledge of reality, nor you bother to see 'whether the beliefs you hold are according to the truth or not.
Secondly, it is told that: Allah SWT is the Creator and Sovereign of the entire Universe.
Thirdly, a few basic principles from Prophets Abraham and Musa have been reiterated so that people understand that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) has not brought a new and novel religion rather they should know that these fundamental truths are those that the former Prophets of Allah SWT have been presenting in their respective ages.
The Surah concludes, thus: "The Hour of Judgment has approached near. Before the occurrence of that Hour, you are being warned through Muhammad (PBUH) and the Quran just as the former nations had been warned before. Now, if it is this warning that you find novel and strange? Which you mock and ridicule?? Abandon this attitude and bow down to Allah SWT and serve Him alone!" Upon hearing this impressive conclusion even, the most hardened deniers of Truth were completely overwhelmed, and when after reciting these Ayats of Divine Word the Holy Messenger of Allah (PBUH) fell in prostration, they too could not help falling in prostration along with him.
SAJDAH TILAWAT Ayat 62

commentary.text:
This is about the Holy Prophet’s second meeting with Angel Gabriel in which he appeared before him in his real shape and nature. The place where this meeting took place has been described as Sidrat-al-muntaha, along with which it has been said that nearby it is located Jannat-al-mava (Garden of Repose). 

Sidrah in Arabic means the lote-tree and muntaha the extreme edge or limit. Thus, literally, sidrat-al-muntaha means the lote-tree that is situated on the extreme edge or limit -- whatever is beyond it is known to none but Allah SWT. These are the mysteries of the divine universe which are incomprehensible for us.

translation.text: The ˹Prophet’s˺ sight never wandered, nor did it overreach.

commentary.text: Despite all the amazing scenes and splendor on display the Prophet (PBUH) was in complete control of himself and totally attentive. He kept his mind and his sight focused upon the object for which he had been summoned and did not let his sight wander (like a spectator) to have a glimpse of the wonderful objects present there.

This can be understood by the example of a person who gets an opportunity to be present in the court of a mighty and powerful king, where he comes across such glory and splendor that had never even been conceived by him before. Now, if he is a weak or insubstantial person, he would be struck with amazement, un-initiated in the court etiquette, he would become heedless of the royal presence and turn his gaze to every side staring at the embellishments of the court.

But a noble, reverent and dutiful person will neither be stupefied and confounded, nor will become lost in witnessing the court, rather he will present himself with full dignity and will keep his mind concentrated on the object for which he had been summoned in the royal court.
This very virtue and quality of the Prophet (PBUH) have been honored in this Ayat.
Lesson: There is a necessary focus required to study the Quran. Develop this quality to receive.

translation.text: He certainly saw some of his Lord’s greatest signs.

Most are of the opinion that this Ayat and Ayat 31 of Surah An-Nisa classify sins into two main kinds: the major sins and the minor sins, and these two Ayats give man the hope that if he abstains from the major sins and open indecencies, Allah SWT will overlook his minor errors. 

As for the question, what is the distinction between the major and the minor sins, and what kinds of sins are major and what kinds of them minor? Every such act is a major sin which has been forbidden by a clear ordinance of the divine Book and the Shariah of the Prophet (PBUH), or for which Allah and His Messenger (PBUH) have prescribed a punishment in the world or have held out a threat of punishment in the Hereafter. Shirk, Riba, Zina, Murder, Lying are some of the major sins.
Apart from this class of sins all other acts which are disapproved by the Shariah, come under the definition of minor sins.
Lastly don’t assume you are pious or brag about your religiosity. Only Allah SWT.

commentary.text: This Ayat refers to Walid ibn al-Mughirah, a powerful Qurayshi leader who was close to accepting Islam. A pagan friend talked him out of it, offering to “take responsibility” for his punishment in the Hereafter in exchange for money. Walid agreed, paid only a small amount, then backed out of Islam completely.

The Quran highlights this story to expose how absurd and reckless such thinking is. No one can carry another person’s accountability before Allah SWT, and treating the Hereafter like a financial transaction only shows how deeply misguided and careless these people were about divine truth.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the very first verse Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The incident of the (splitting of the moon) that has been mentioned which determines its period of revelation precisely. This incident took place at Mina in Makkah about five years before the Holy Prophet's migration to Madinah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The splitting of the Moon was a manifest sign that the Day of Resurrection, is fast approaching.
The Moon physically split into two distinct parts and for on-lookers one part appeared on one side of the mountain while the other on the other side of it. Then, in an instant the two rejoined.
This was a manifest proof that the system of the Universe could be disrupted. Huge stars and Planets could split asunder, disintegrate, collide with each other similarly the Day of Resurrection, could also and will happen.
In the end, the disbelievers have been told that Allah SWT does not need to make lengthy preparations to bring about Resurrection. With His simple command it will take place immediately. Everything in the Universe and with mankind happens at its own appointed time. It cannot be that whenever somebody gives a challenge, Resurrection is brought about to convince him.
This Surah is powerful, direct and creates a sense of urgency.

sections.title: 1-8 THE DAY OF JUDGMENT IS DRAWING NEAR YET THE UNBELIEVERS ARE NOT PAYING HEED TO THE SIGNS OF ALLAH

translation.text: The Hour has drawn near and the moon was split ˹in two˺.

commentary.text: The Quran presents it as a SIGN OF RESURRECTION, and A MIRACLE OF PROPHETHOOD — though it still affirmed the Prophet’s truthfulness. There is a sense of urgency that the hour is fast approaching.

Reliable Hadith narrations confirm that people saw the moon split in two parts around five years before the Hijrah, and then it rejoined. Some companions were eyewitnesses; others reported what they heard from elders. The Prophet (PBUH) split the moon with his finger.
Lesson: Strive and strive hard with the Quran as time is of the essence. Each person will have nothing but his effort and striving on the DoJ.

translation.text: Yet, whenever they see a sign, they turn away, saying, “Same old magic!”
They rejected ˹the truth˺ and followed their own desires—and every matter will be settled—

commentary.text: The mushrqeen of Mecca demanded miracles from the Prophet (PBUH). They persisted in denying the Hereafter even after having witnessed this manifest sign, mainly because it clashed with their desires of the flesh.
The Quran contradicts their desires therefore they called the miracle magic and a trick.

All affairs ultimately must reach an appointed end. Thus, the inevitable conflict between the disbelievers and Muhammad (PBUH) has to reach an end. A time will certainly come when it will be clearly established the worshipers of the truth shall one day see the result of their worshiping the truth and the worshipers of falsehood of their worshiping the falsehood.
Lesson: Literal meaning of desire in Arabic is to fall. Desires can make people stoop to very low levels.

translation.text: even though the stories ˹of destroyed nations˺ that have already come to them are a sufficient deterrent.

commentary.text: In the Quran, there has come to them the news of the earlier nations that disbelieved in their Messengers and as a result the torment, punishment and affliction upon them.
Lesson: The best way to learn is by not emulating mistakes made by others. Take heed from them.

translation.text: ˹This Quran is˺ profound ˹in˺ wisdom, but warnings are of no benefit ˹to them˺.

commentary.text: The Quran Is Enough Of A Miracle. It contains perfect wisdom and balance.

translation.text: So turn away from them ˹O Prophet˺. ˹And wait for˺ the Day ˹when˺ the caller will summon ˹them˺ for something horrifying.

commentary.text: Prophet (PBUH) is being told to leave them or turn away from the obstinate disbelievers. When every effort has been made to make them understand the truth, including citing examples about the consequence of their rejecting the Prophetic messages, if they are still disinclined to give up their stubbornness, then they should be left alone.

Now, they will believe only after death when they arise from their graves to see with their own eyes that the Resurrection of which they were being forewarned and exhorted to adopt the truth, had taken place.

translation.text: With eyes downcast, they will come forth from the graves as if they were swarming locusts,

commentary.text:
Literally means their eyes or their looks will be downcast. This can have several meanings:

(1) That they will appear terror-stricken. 
(2) That they will be reflecting disgrace and humiliation, for as soon as they arise out of their graves they would realize that it was indeed the same second life which they had been denying, for which they had made no preparation, and in which they would have to present themselves before their God as culprits.
(3) That with awe-struck looks they would be watching the dreadful scenes before them, from which they would not be able to avert their eyes.

commentary.text:

The disbelievers will say: “This is a hard Day.", meaning, `this is a hard, terrible, horrifying and distressful Day,'
Lesson: On the DoJ even before the verdict has been delivered we all will know where we stand.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: This Surah is entitled Ar Rahman, the word with which it begins. This title, however, deeply relates to the subject matter of the Surah too, for in it, from the beginning to the end, the manifestations of Allah' SWTs attribute of mercy and grace have been mentioned.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Surah Ar-Rahmān is a Makki Surah, revealed in the early years of Prophethood, well before Hijrah.
It was recited both to Quraysh (by Ibn Masʿud) and to the jinn (who responded better than humans). Surah Ar-Rahmān was among the first Surahs recited publicly in Makkah. It is a pair with Surah Waqiah (next surah).
The Holy Prophet said the jinn gathered to hear the Quran. They responded to it better than you have. As I recited the Divine Words, ("O jinn and men, which blessings of your Lord will you deny?") they would respond to it, saying: O our Lord, do not deny any of your blessings Praise is for You alone'!" This happened in the 10th year of the Prophethood when the Holy Prophet had halted at Makkah on his way back from Ta'if.

items.text:
This is the only Surah of the Quran in which besides men the jinn also -- who are the other creation of the earth endowed with freedom of will and action -- have been directly addressed, and both men and jinn have been made to realize the wonders of Allah SWT's power, His countless blessings, along with man and jinns own helplessness and accountability before Him.
Thus, the Surah moves in a rhythm — blessings, warnings, punishments, rewards — always circling back to the refrain that challenges denial and ingratitude. Its eloquence, balance, and repetition are designed to pierce hearts and awaken conscience.
This is also called the Surah of Blessings. Surah Rehman describes the many blessings of Allah SWT. Allah SWT says you don’t need miracles to understand or recognize your Raab rather just look around you – there are signs and miracles all around.
فَبِاَىِّ اٰلَاۤءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبٰنِ

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah name is from the very first Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Surah Al-Wāqiʿah was revealed in the early Makkan period, after Surah Ṭā Hā and before Ash-Shuʿarāʾ, and evidence from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab’s conversion in the fifth year of Prophethood confirms its early revelation. It is a pair with Surah Ar Rehman.

items.text:
The central theme is the certainty of the Hereafter, and the refutation of the disbelievers’ doubts about Resurrection and the Quran. The Surah declares that when the inevitable event occurs, no one will be able to deny or avert it.
Humanity will be divided into three groups:
The Foremost (closest to Allah),
The People of the Right (the righteous),
The People of the Left (the deniers and sinners).
It describes in detail the rewards of the first two groups and the punishments of the last.

The Surah then presents proofs of Tawhid and the Hereafter by drawing attention to creation, food, water, and fire—reminding humans of their utter dependence on Allah and His power to recreate them after death.
It also defends the divine origin of the Qur’an, emphasizing that it is preserved in the well-guarded Tablet and delivered only through pure angels, not devils.

The Surah concludes by reminding man of death as the ultimate proof of helplessness: if humans cannot prevent death or restore a soul, how can they deny Allah’s power to resurrect and judge? Each soul, at death, will see the outcome destined for it—whether bliss, peace, or punishment.

sections.title: 1-26 SCENE OF THE DOOMSDAY WHEN MANKIND WILL BE DIVIDED INTO THREE GROUPS, A REWARD FOR THE FOREHAND GROUP

translation.text: When the Inevitable Event takes place,

commentary.text: Allah SWT says, Al-Waqi`ah (the occurrence or the Event), is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, because that Day is real and will surely occur. The Day of Judgment is near and a certainty. It will be a very Major Event.

Also see: (69:15)
Then on that Day shall the Waqi`ah occur.

translation.text: – and then there will be no one to deny its occurrence
It will debase ˹some˺ and elevate ˹others˺.

commentary.text: This Day will upset every order and turn things upside-down, that is, judgments or verdicts regarding who is considered elite or noble and those who are considered lowly/ or disgraced will be made on quite a different basis in the Hereafter. THE ONLY CRITERIA BEING IMAN WHICH WILL ELEVATE OR DEBASE A PERSON IN THE HEREAFTER.
Lesson: REDEFINE SUCCESS IN YOUR MIND.
DoJ begins right after death. Each will know exactly where their next destination will be.

translation.text: When the earth will be violently shaken,
and the mountains will be crushed to pieces,
becoming scattered ˹particles of˺ dust,
you will ˹all˺ be ˹divided into˺ three groups:

commentary.text: Entire mankind is addressed. All human beings who have been born since the first day of creation and will be born till the Day of Resurrection will ultimately be divided into three groups or categories.

translation.text: the people of the right, how ˹blessed˺ will they be;

commentary.text: Those of the right hand. This, however, does not imply its lexical meaning, but it signifies the people of exalted rank and position. The Arabs regarded the right hand as a symbol of strength and eminence and honor and therefore would seat a person whom they wished to do honor, on the right hand, in the assemblies.
Thus, these are the fortunate and blessed people.

translation.text: the people of the left, how ˹miserable˺ will they be;

commentary.text: The Arabs regarded shimal (the left hand) and shum (bad omen) as synonyms, the left hand being a symbol of weakness and indignity.
Therefore, ashab-almashamah implies ill-omened people, or those who would suffer disgrace and ignominy, and would be made to stand on the left side in the Court of Allah.

translation.text: and the foremost ˹in faith˺ will be the foremost ˹in Paradise˺.

commentary.text: The Sābiqūn are those who excel in faith, virtue, and good deeds—responding earliest to Allah’ SWTs call, leading in charity, jihad, service, and truth. The trend setters. Those who don’t wait or follow rather they lead. Like Khadija, Abu Bakr etc. May Allah Be Pleased with Them.
On the Day of Resurrection, mankind will be divided into three groups:
the righteous on the right,
the wicked on the left, and

the Sābiqūn at the forefront, nearest to Allah SWT. A hadith explains that they are those who accepted truth immediately, fulfilled others’ rights willingly, and judged with justice as for themselves.

translation.text: They are the ones nearest ˹to Allah˺,

commentary.text: This is what Allah SWT wants for us that is, to be near Him. So those who strove hard to be near Allah SWT in this world will be of those who are near Him in the Hereafter as well.
Lesson: Money, power, etc., comes with striving so strive for the best, that is, strive and work hard to be near Allah SWT.

translation.text: in the Gardens of Bliss.
˹They will be˺ a multitude from earlier generations
and a few from later generations.

commentary.text: The commentators differ about who the “former” and “latter” people refer to. Some say the former are all the communities from Prophet Adam (AS) up to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the latter are those who lived from his time until the Day of Judgment—meaning earlier nations had more of the foremost in faith.

Others say the Ayat refers only to the Prophet’s ummah, with the earliest Muslims counted as the former and later generations as the latter, the former having more of the foremost. A third view is that it applies to every Prophet’s followers, where the earliest believers were greater in number than those who came later.

Hadith: Some of the poor companions went to the Prophet (PBUH) and asked how they can compete with the rich companions who give a lot in charity while also doing all the other obligations. Prophet (PBUH) told them to recite Tashbeeh Fatima after every salah. 33 Subhan Allah, 33 AH and 34 Allah hu Akbar.
LESSON: I MUST NOT GET UP RIGHT AFTER SALAH.

All three interpretations are possible, and the underlying message is that while human populations have increased, the proportion of the truly foremost in faith and good deeds has become smaller over time.

translation.text: ˹All will be˺ on jeweled thrones,
reclining face to face.
They will be waited on by eternal youths
with cups, pitchers, and a drink ˹of pure wine˺ from a flowing stream,
that will cause them neither headache nor intoxication.

commentary.text: Unlike worldly wine that causes these afflictions.

translation.text: ˹They will also be served˺ any fruit they choose
and meat from any bird they desire.
And ˹they will have˺ maidens with gorgeous eyes
like pristine pearls,
˹all˺ as a reward for what they used to do.

commentary.text: Allah SWT says that these delights that We granted them are rewards for the good deeds that they performed (in this life).

translation.text: There they will never hear any idle or sinful talk—

commentary.text: This is one of the major blessings of Paradise, which has been mentioned at several places in the Quran, that in Paradise human ears will remain secure against idle and frivolous talk, lying, backbiting slander, invective, boasting and bragging, taunts and mockery, satire and sarcasm.

It will not be a society of foul-mouthed, indecent people who will throw mud at each other, but a society of noble and civilized people free of such frivolities. A person who has been blessed with some decency of manner and sense by Allah SWT can very well feel what an agony it is in worldly life, a hope of deliverance from which has been given to man in Paradise.

translation.text: only good and virtuous speech.

commentary.text:
No Laghw (evil vain talk) will they hear therein, nor any sinful speech. But only the saying of "Salaman (peace).
Meaning they will not hear foul or unnecessary speech in Paradise.
Thus far the description of Heaven: Perfect location; Utmost comfort, Perfect company, wonderful food, Great service, Good conversation.

translation.text: And the people of the right—how ˹blessed˺ will they be!

commentary.text: Allah SWT first (above) mentioned the final destination of those foremost in faith, the nearest to Him, the sabiqoon.
Now Allah SWT mentions the reward for a second group of people, that is, those on the right, the righteous believers.

translation.text: ˹They will be˺ amid thornless lote trees,
clusters of bananas,
extended shade,
flowing water,
abundant fruit—
never out of season nor forbidden—
and elevated furnishings.

commentary.text: And on couches, raised high, meaning, high, soft and comfortable.

translation.text: Indeed, We will have perfectly created their mates,
making them virgins,

commentary.text: This Ayat refers to the virtuous women of the world who will enter Paradise by virtue of their faith and deeds. Allah SWT will renew them in beauty and youth, making them pure and virgins regardless of their age, appearance, or marital status at death. If their husbands also enter Paradise, they will be reunited; otherwise, they will be married to other dwellers of Paradise.

translation.text: loving and of equal age,

commentary.text: The word uruban is used for the best feminine qualities of the woman in Arabic. This signifies a woman who is graceful and elegant, well-mannered and eloquent, and brimful of feminine feelings, who loves her husband with all her heart, and whose husband also loves her with all his heart.

This Ayat indicates that the women of Paradise will be of equal age, either with their husbands or among themselves, or both. All will remain eternally young and beautiful. Supporting Hadith describe that the people of Paradise will be around 33 years old, fair, handsome, strong, and adorned with radiant features, symbolizing eternal youth and perfection.

translation.text: for the people of the right,
a large throng from the ancients,
and also a large throng from those of later times.

commentary.text: When the earlier Ayat 13 and 14 said that only a few from later generations would be among the foremost, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (RA) wept, fearing that few Muslims would be saved. In response, Allah SWT revealed Ayat 39 and 40, assuring that there would be a multitude from both earlier and later generations. The Prophet (PBUH) comforted ʿUmar with this revelation, explaining that from Adam (AS) until him there would be many saved, and from him until the Day of Judgment there would also be many saved.
May we be people of the right and may we be of the sabiqoon. Ameen. When asking for Heaven always AIM HIGH! Ask for Jannat ul Firdaus.

commentary.text: This Ayat emphasizes that just as birth is under Allah SWT’s control, so is death. He alone decides who dies in the womb, in infancy, or later in life. No power can delay or hasten a person’s appointed time of death, and neither medical expertise nor human foresight can prevent or predict it. Reflect on these creations and appreciate/recognize the wonders all around us.

The Quran condemned idol-worship and unjust practices. The Quraysh elite controlled trade, pilgrimage, and idol-related income in Makkah. If people accepted Islam’s message of Tawḥīd and justice, their idols would lose importance, their authority would weaken, and their profits would shrink. So, instead of seeing the Quran as guidance, they saw it as a threat to their business and status.
In short: They denied truth to protect their worldly interests.

commentary.text: When a righteous believer dies, the angels greet the soul with the words: “O pure soul in a good body, come to Rawḥ and Rayḥān and to a Lord Who is pleased, not angry.”

Scholars explain Rawḥ to mean rest, mercy, and peace—freedom from the hardships of the world—and Rayḥān to mean provision, joy, and fragrance from Paradise. Together they signify comfort, mercy, and glad tidings for the soul at death.

The believer’s soul is welcomed with peace and reassurance, while martyrs’ souls live freely in the form of green birds in Paradise. Those who love to meet Allah SWT at that moment find Allah SWT eager to meet them; those who fear and reject Him receive the opposite fate—punishment and loss.
In short: Rawḥ and Rayḥān represent peace, mercy, and blissful welcome for the righteous soul as it begins its eternal journey to Paradise.
May we be of those who reach this level. Ameen.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from Ayat 25.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Ḥadīd is unanimously a Madani Surah, revealed after the Prophet (PBUH) migrated to Madinah. Its content suggests it was revealed between the Battle of Uhud and the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (around the 4th–5th year after Hijrah).
At that time, the small Muslim community in Madinah was surrounded by enemies and struggling for survival. The Surah was revealed to urge believers to sacrifice both wealth and life for the cause of Islam. This is supported by Ayat 10, which praises those who spent and fought before victory as being superior to those who did so later.
Thus, the Surah came at a critical stage, calling Muslims to strengthen their faith through sincere action, courage, and financial support.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Ḥadīd teaches that true faith demands sacrifice and sincerity, not mere words. It calls believers to give, strive, and trust in Allah SWT —reminding them that worldly life is fleeting, but the reward for those who act for Allah SWT’s sake is everlasting light and mercy.
The Surah urges Muslims to spend in the way of Allah SWT, especially during times of struggle for the survival of Islam. True faith is not just words or rituals—it requires sincerity, sacrifice, and devotion. Wealth is a trust from Allah SWT, and only what is spent for His cause truly benefits a person.
Believers should remain humble in prosperity and patient in hardship, unlike hypocrites who are proud when blessed and stingy when asked to give.
Allah SWT sent Prophets, Books, and justice to guide humanity and iron (power) to defend the truth. These trials are meant to test who truly supports Allah’s religion.
Listen to Dr Israr about the timings and seqencec.

sections.title: 1-10 ALL THAT IS IN THE HEAVENS AND EARTH GLORIFIES ALLAH, WHO CREATED THE HEAVENS AND EARTH IN SIX PERIODS AND HAS THE KNOWLEDGE OF EVERYTHING AND THOSE WHO SPEND IN CHARITY WILL BE RICHLY REWARDED

arabic_lines: سَبَّحَ لِلّٰهِ مَا فِى السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالۡاَرۡضِۚ وَهُوَ الۡعَزِيۡزُ الۡحَكِيۡمُ

translation.text: Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, for He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

commentary.text: Every part of creation—past, present, and future—declares Allah SWT’s perfection and greatness. (Verbally and non-verbally).

This Ayat means that Allah alone is truly All-Mighty (Al-‘Azīz) and All-Wise (Al-Ḥakīm). His power is absolute—no one can resist or change His decisions—but He uses that power with perfect wisdom, knowledge, mercy, and justice. The Quran pairs “Al-‘Azīz” with attributes like All-Wise, All-Knowing, Merciful, and Forgiving to show that Allah’s infinite power is never harsh or unjust but always guided by wisdom and goodness.
Hadith: Hazrat Fatima asked her father Prophet (PBUH) that she need a maid the Prophet (PBUH) told her to do tashbeeh. Basically, ask Allah SWT for any and everything and rely only and soley on Him.
Tasbeeh Fatima is SA 33, AH 33, Allah hu Akbar 34 times.

translation.text: He is the First and the Last, the Most High and Most Near, and He has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

commentary.text: More attributes of Allah SWT. Allah SWT is eternal. Noone is above Him in any sense. He is most near to His Servant (closer to us than our jugular vein).

Lesson: Allah SWT is aware of our inner most thoughts and can hear even our whisper when we speak to Him. We are never alone. No matter what time or what state. When we read our salah it is a dialogue and not a monologue.

translation.text: He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself on the Throne. He knows all that enters the earth and all that comes forth from it, and all that comes down from the heaven and all that goes up to it. He is with you wherever you are. Allah sees all that you do.

commentary.text: Allah SWT states that He created the heavens and earth, and all that is between them, in six Days and then rose (Istawa) over the Throne after He created them. We discussed this before in the explanation of Surah Al-A`raf.
Allah SWT didn’t just leave His creation rather is witnessing everything and helping and assisting, for example, when Prophet Musa was afraid to go to Pharon, Allah SWT said, ‘I am with you.’
Allah SWT is with the people of (i) taqwa (ii) patience (iii) who believe (iv) who do Ahsaan. These are the qualities on should develop to expect Allah SWT’s help.

translation.text: Believe in Allah and in His Messenger and expend of what He has entrusted to you. A great reward awaits those of you who believe and spend their wealth.

commentary.text: True faith is proven through action and sacrifice, not just belief in words. Wealth (our money, time, energy etc) is a temporary trust, and what truly benefits a person is that is spent for Allah’s sake.
IMAN + SPENDING IN ALLAH WAY = SUCCESS

SPENDING IN ALLAH’S CAUSE: “Spending” here means supporting the struggle for Islam, especially helping to fund the defense of the Muslim community and aiding the persecuted Muslims who had migrated to Madinah. At that time, Islam needed both material and moral support.

WEALTH IS A TRUST FROM ALLAH SWT: The Ayat reminds believers that their wealth (money, time, energy etc.) belongs to Allah SWT, and they are only trustees or caretakers. So, they should spend it for Allah’s sake while they can, as what is spent in His path is what truly remains forever in reward.
The Prophet (PBUH) said: “Whatever you give for Allah’s sake is what you have really saved.” (Bukhari, Muslim)

translation.text: And why should you not spend in the cause of Allah, while Allah is the ˹sole˺ inheritor of the heavens and the earth? Those of you who donated and fought before the victory ˹over Mecca˺ are unparalleled. They are far greater in rank than those who donated and fought afterwards. Yet Allah has promised each a fine reward. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

commentary.text: This Ayat was revealed about Abu Bakr al Siddiq who gave everything he had for Allah SW. Those who gave and fought for Islam before victory—when Muslims were weak and faced real danger—are higher in rank than those who contributed after success. Their sacrifices were greater because they supported Islam when it seemed most at risk.

This Ayat reminds believers that all wealth belongs to Allah SWT, and after death, He alone will inherit everything. So, it is wiser to spend in Allah’s cause now and earn reward, rather than leave it behind with no benefit in the Hereafter. Believers should not fear poverty, for Allah SWT owns the treasures of the heavens and the earth and always provides more. Spend willingly in Allah’s cause while you can

sections.title: 11-19 ON THAT DAY THE TRUE BELIEVERS WILL HAVE THEIR LIGHT SHINING BEFORE THEM WHILE THE HYPOCRITES WILL HAVE THEIR FATE NO DIFFERENT THAN THE DISBELIEVERS AND THOSE WHO SPEND IN CHARITY WILL BE REPAID MANYFOLD AND ALSO BE GIVEN LIBERAL REWARD BESIDES IT

translation.text: Who is it that will give Allah a beautiful loan? A loan that Allah will repay after increasing it many times and grant him a generous reward.

commentary.text: Also see Ayat 18

Invitation to step forward to something good. Allah SWT is so Generous and Kind that when a believer spends from the wealth Allah SWT Himself has given, He calls it a “loan to Allah SWT.” This “good loan” means any sincere act of giving for Allah SWT’s sake/cause (can be money for orphans, masjid, widows, community work etc. but also means ones time, energy, knowledge and the like)—without pride, showing off, or personal gain—only seeking His pleasure. The intention is key.
Allah SWT makes two promises to those who give sincerely:
He will return it multiplied many times over, and
He will grant an extra reward from Himself in the Hereafter.

The story of Abu Dahdah (RA) beautifully shows this spirit. When he heard this Ayat, he immediately offered his entire garden—with 600 date palms—as a loan to Allah SWT, and his wife joyfully supported his decision.
WHEN YOU GIVE SINCERELY FOR ALLAH SWT’S SAKE, IT IS NOT A LOSS—IT IS AN INVESTMENT WITH GUARANTEED, MULTIPLIED REWARD FROM THE MOST GENEROUS.
Lesson: Qard ḥasan is devotion. So it is unlike Zakat which is obligatory.

translation.text: On that Day you will see believing men and women that their light will be running before them and on their right hands. (They will be told): “A good tiding to you today.” There shall be Gardens beneath which rivers flow; therein they shall abide. That indeed is the great triumph.

commentary.text: This Ayat and the ones that follow describe that on the Day of Judgment. (Pul Sirat or the Bridge we all will have to cross).

Light will be granted only to the true believers. This light is not just a spiritual metaphor; it's a tangible guide, illuminating their path. The "light" (noor) is described as running forward before them.
This light will be the reflection of one’s faith and righteous deeds—the more sincere and good one’s actions were in life, the brighter his light will be in the Hereafter.

translation.text: On that Day hypocrite men and women will beg the believers, “Wait for us so that we may have some of your light.” It will be said ˹mockingly˺, “Go back ˹to the world˺ and seek a light ˹there˺!” Then a ˹separating˺ wall with a gate will be erected between them. On the near side will be grace and on the far side will be torment.

commentary.text: It means that when the believers will be going towards Paradise, the light will be before them, and the hypocrites will be stumbling about in the darkness behind. At that time, they will call out to the believers, who lived with them together in the same Muslim society in the world, saying: Look back towards us awhile so that we also may get some light.

The people of Paradise will enter it through a gate and then the gate will be closed. On one side of the gate there will be the blessings of Paradise and on the other the torment of Hell. For the hypocrites it will not be possible to cross the barrier that will stand between them and Paradise.
The disbelievers, and hypocrites, will remain in darkness, just as they were blind to the truth in the world.

translation.text: The tormented will cry out to those graced, “Were we not with you?” They will reply, “Yes ˹you were˺. But you chose to be tempted ˹by hypocrisy˺, ˹eagerly˺ awaited ˹our demise˺, doubted ˹the truth˺, and were deluded by false hopes until Allah’s decree ˹of your death˺ came to pass. And ˹so˺ the Chief Deceiver deceived you about Allah.

commentary.text: These Ayat describe the conversation between the believers and the hypocrites on the Day of Judgment, explaining why they will be separated despite having lived together in this world.
The hypocrites will protest, saying: “Did we not live among you, pray, fast, give zakat, perform Hajj, and share ties of family and community? Why are we separated today?”

Although the hypocrites appeared Muslim outwardly and were physically present for worship, they never had sincere faith. Their hearts remained attached to disbelief, and they only followed Islam when it suited their worldly interests.

The Quran describes their attitude as tarabbus—waiting on the sidelines. They neither fully joined the believers nor openly opposed them, but stayed neutral, watching to see who would win. Their hesitation came from doubt and disbelief: and were driven only by worldly desires. Satan deceived them with false hopes and kept them away from sincere faith.
In short, these Ayats expose the inner reality of hypocrisy: living among believers but inwardly ruled by doubt, self-interest, and Satan’s deception.
In this world they were all mixed together but, in the Hereafter, they will be completely separate.
Qualities of a hypocrite: Hypocrites wait and delay. They doubt and are deluded by false hopes and expectations of salvation. Allah SWT will forgive all.
Hypocrites’ sins become inconsequential.
For a believer a sin is a big thing. A believer should find ways to constantly renew and strengthen his faith and spend in Allah SWT’s way.

translation.text: So Today no ransom will be accepted from you ˹hypocrites˺, nor from the disbelievers. Your home is the Fire—it is the ˹only˺ fitting place for you. What an evil destination!”

commentary.text: This Clearly Shows That In The Hereafter The Hypocrites Will Be Doomed To The Same Fate As The Disbelievers.
This Ayat stresses the impossibility of offering any form of compensation or ransom to avoid the destined outcome for both hypocrites and disbelievers.

translation.text: Indeed, those men and women who give in charity and lend to Allah a good loan will have it multiplied for them, and they will have an honourable reward.

commentary.text: Also see Ayat 11

Sadaqah, as an Islamic term, is the charity given sincerely and with a pure intention only with a view to seek Allah’ SWT’s good pleasure. The word is derived from sidq, therefore, sadaqat (sincerity) is of its essence.
Theirs will be a generous, handsome reward, a good dwelling to return to and an honorable final destination.
Lesson: Qard ḥasan is devotion. So it is unlike Zakat which is obligatory.

arabic_lines: وَالَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا بِاللّٰهِ وَرُسُلِهٖۤ اُولٰٓـئِكَ هُمُ الصِّدِّيۡقُوۡنَۖ وَالشُّهَدَآ

translation.text: ˹As for˺ those who believe in Allah and His messengers, it is they who are ˹truly˺ the people of truth. And the martyrs, with their Lord, will have their reward and their light. But ˹as for˺ those who disbelieve and reject Our signs, it is they who will be the residents of the Hellfire.

commentary.text: These Ayats describe the true believers and their ranks in the sight of Allah SWT. The believers here are those who were sincere in faith, sacrificed their wealth and lives for Allah’s cause, and remained steadfast under all circumstances.

The term “Ṣiddīq” (most truthful) refers to a believer whose faith, words, and actions are in complete harmony. He not only speaks the truth but lives by it with full sincerity and loyalty, never wavering in his commitment to Allah and His Messenger (PBUH). Such a person’s life reflects faithfulness, integrity, and righteousness.

The word “Shahīd,” originally means “a witness to the truth.” Every sincere believer is a witness because they testify to Islam through their faith, character, and actions. A martyr is a specific type of shahīd who gives their life in Allah SWT’s cause. All martyrs are witnesses, but not all witnesses are martyrs. Allah SWT has promised each group reward and light according to their sincerity, while those who deny His signs will face the Fire.

In the end, Allah SWT promises that each believer — whether Siddīq or Shahīd — will receive their own reward and light in the Hereafter, according to their faith, sincerity, and deeds. Everyone’s light and rank will match the degree of their devotion and sacrifice for Allah SWT’s cause.

sections.title: 20-25 LIFE OF THIS WORLD IS BUT A PLAY, AMUSEMENT AND ILLUSION AND

translation.text: Know that this worldly life is no more than play, amusement, luxury, mutual boasting, and competition in wealth and children. This is like rain that causes plants to grow, to the delight of the planters. But later the plants dry up and you see them wither, then they are reduced to chaff. And in the Hereafter there will be either severe punishment or forgiveness and pleasure of Allah, whereas the life of this world is no more than the delusion of enjoyment.

commentary.text: This Ayat reminds us that the life of this world is fleeting and deceptive, while the life of the Hereafter is real, lasting, and far more valuable. The Quran repeatedly emphasizes that worldly pleasures—such as wealth, beauty, status, and possessions—are temporary attractions meant to test human priorities. People, due to short-sightedness, often mistake these fleeting comforts for true success, forgetting that a single twist of fate can end them instantly.
In contrast, the Hereafter is eternal: its joys and rewards are everlasting, and its losses are severe and permanent.

True success lies not in accumulating worldly gains but in earning Allah SWT’s forgiveness and pleasure, which bring eternal peace and fulfillment. Compared to that, even the greatest worldly wealth and power appear trivial.

Life in this world described as (i) play, (ii) amusement, (iii) luxury, (iv) mutual boasting, and (v) competition in wealth and children. Like a plant that grows tall and strong much to the delight of the farmer but then wilts and dies. This life too will not last long. The message is clear: the wise person invests in the Hereafter, while the one who clings to the temporary glitter of this life only deceives himself.
Lesson: Allah SWT says we should know. ‘Know that this worldly…’ so gain knowledge as it brings conviction.
Also understand that company affects us in the pursuit to keep up with the Jones.

arabic_lines: سَابِقُوا اِلٰى مَغۡفِرَةٍ مِّنۡ رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا كَعَرۡضِ السَّمَآءِ وَ الۡاَرۡضِۙ

translation.text: ˹So˺ compete with one another for forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. This is the favour of Allah. He grants it to whoever He wills. And Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty.

commentary.text: This Ayat teaches that instead of competing for worldly gains—such as wealth, status, and material pleasures—believers should race towards and compete in doing good deeds that lead to Allah SWT’s forgiveness and Paradise.

True success lies not in worldly superiority but in excelling in faith, charity, sincerity, and righteousness. Thus, we are urged to shift our focus from temporary achievements to the eternal reward of Allah SWT’s mercy and the everlasting joy of Paradise.

The vastness of Paradise is being described emphasizing that it is far beyond human imagination. The word ard (translated as “earth” or “land”) here refers not just to physical breadth but to boundless spaciousness. The purpose is not to measure Paradise’s size but to help us grasp its limitless expanse and grandeur. The Quran compares its vastness to that of the heavens and the earth combined, showing that Paradise is not confined like worldly homes—it is an entire universe of endless beauty and freedom.

When Surah Al-Ḥadīd and Surah Āl ʿImrān are read together, it becomes clear that the believer’s home in Paradise will not be a restricted space but an infinite realm open to exploration and delight. Unlike in this world, where travel beyond our planet demands immense struggle and resources, in the Hereafter the righteous will move and see with ease whatever they wish. Thus, the Ayat gives a glimpse of the immense generosity and freedom that await those who earn Allah SWT’s pleasure.

translation.text: No calamity ˹or blessing˺ occurs on earth or in yourselves without being ˹written˺ in a Record before We bring it into being. This is certainly easy for Allah.

commentary.text: There is nothing that touches you or happens in existence, but it is inscribed in the Book of Decrees before `before We created the creation and started life. It is predestined and divine preordained by Allah SWT. So, a believer embraces patience and gratitude because everything is part of a divine plan. This fosters a sense of trust and tranquility in Allah SWT’s divine plan.
This is said after describing the world because the world is full of trials as well as blessings – all predestined for us. Realize life is temporary and base decisions on the Hereafter.
Remember what hits you was never meant to miss you and what misses you was never meant to reach you.

translation.text: ˹We let you know this˺ so that you neither grieve over what you have missed nor boast over what He has granted you. For Allah does not like whoever is arrogant, boastful—

commentary.text: Allah SWT reminds them that every hardship we face is not accidental, but part of His divine plan, already written in the Book of Destiny. These difficulties are meant for their training and purification, preparing them for the great mission and responsibility ahead. Without such trials, they would lack the strength, patience, and spiritual depth needed to handle future power and success. This Ayat was revealed to comfort and strengthen the Muslims during a time of great hardship.

Thus, the Ayat teaches us that tests are not signs of rejection, but of divine preparation—a necessary process to build strong, resilient believers capable of upholding truth in the face of all adversity.
Don’t grieve for what has missed you, i.e., opportunities, things etc. Similarly, do not be proud with what Allah SWT has bestowed on you, rather be grateful for what you have.
Never say I deserve this… Remain humble and remember this is all decreed for a reason – a test.
Traits disliked by Allah SWT: Arrogance and Boastfulness. And grieving/longing for what we don’t have.

translation.text: those who are stingy and promote stinginess among people. And whoever turns away ˹should know that˺ Allah ˹alone˺ is truly the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

commentary.text: These Ayats expose the true nature of the hypocrites within the Muslim community. Outwardly, they appeared to be believers—they prayed, spoke of faith, and mingled with sincere Muslims—but inwardly they lacked sincerity. The small amount of wealth, influence, or position they held made them arrogant, and their hearts were filled with stinginess and disbelief in the divine cause.

Not only did they refuse to spend for Allah’s sake, but they also discouraged others, thinking such sacrifices were useless. Their presence among the believers was a test; through hardships and trials, Allah SWT separated the sincere from the insincere, ensuring that only true believers would carry the weight of Islamic leadership.
Traits disliked Allah SWT: Hypocrisy, arrogance, stinginess and disbelief.

Lesson: This Surah invites us to spend. Make you Hereafter and don’t worry about this world. Suffer in the way of Allah SWT; be sleep deprived, be hungry, spend money in Allah SWTs way because none of this will go in vain.  We will benefit as Allah SWT needs nothing from us.

arabic_lines: لَـقَدۡ اَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلَنَا بِالۡبَيِّنٰتِ وَاَنۡزَلۡنَا مَعَهُمُ الۡكِتٰبَ وَالۡمِيۡزَانَ لِيَقُوۡمَ النَّاسُ بِالۡقِسۡطِۚ وَاَنۡزَلۡنَا الۡحَـدِيۡدَ فِيۡهِ بَاۡسٌ شَدِيۡدٌ وَّمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيَـعۡلَمَ اللّٰهُ مَنۡ يَّنۡصُرُهٗ وَ رُسُلَهٗ بِالۡغَيۡبِ ؕ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ قَوِىٌّ عَزِيۡزٌ

translation.text: Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and with them We sent down the Scripture and the balance ˹of justice˺ so that people may administer justice. And We sent down iron with its great might, benefits for humanity, and means for Allah to prove who ˹is willing to˺ stand up for Him and His messengers without seeing Him. Surely Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.

commentary.text: This Ayat beautifully summarizes the purpose of all Prophets and the divine balance between revelation and power. Allah SWT sent His Messengers with three essential things:
clear signs (bayyināt) to prove their truth,
the Book (kitāb) to guide people in all matters of life, and
the Balance (mīzān)—the moral and practical standard for justice and fairness.
So that people could live balanced, fair, and righteous lives. Establish shariah in society. Not just lip service of Islam in society. Revolution/war requires iron (for swords)/strength.

Allah SWT then mentions that He also “sent down iron,” symbolizing strength, power, and authority. This shows that justice cannot be maintained by moral guidance alone; it also requires practical power to protect the right, restrain evil, and ensure peace. Iron here represents both tools for progress and weapons for defense, highlighting the need for strength alongside faith and wisdom. So use the strength and skill that Allah SWT has gifted us. Each one of us has a core competency so use it for Allah SWT’s deen.

Finally, Allah SWT explains that He doesn’t need human help—He is already All-Powerful and Mighty. Rather, He allows this struggle to exist so that human beings can be tested: to see who truly supports truth and justice, and who turns away. This test distinguishes the sincere believers who strive for Allah SWT’s cause from those who merely claim faith without sacrifice.
In short, this Ayat unites spiritual guidance, justice, and strength as the foundation of a just and faithful society.

sections.title: 26-29 PROPHETS NUH, IBRAHIM AND ISA (JESUS) WERE SENT FOR THE GUIDANCE TO THE RIGHT PATH, AS FOR THE MONASTICISM, PEOPLE INSTITUTED IT THEMSELVES

translation.text: And indeed, We sent Noah and Abraham and reserved prophethood and revelation for their descendants. Some of them are ˹rightly˺ guided, while most are rebellious.

Then in the footsteps of these ˹prophets˺, We sent Our messengers, and ˹after them˺ We sent Jesus, son of Mary, and granted him the Gospel, and instilled compassion and mercy into the hearts of his followers. As for monasticism, they made it up—We never ordained it for them—only seeking to please Allah, yet they did not ˹even˺ observe it strictly. So We rewarded those of them who were faithful. But most of them are rebellious.

commentary.text: Allah SWT sent many messengers, and after them, He sent Jesus (PBUH), the son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel. His true followers were known for kindness and mercy. Later, people invented monasticism (living apart from the world in isolation) by themselves—it was not commanded by Allah SWT. They did this thinking it would please Him, but most failed to follow it properly. This Ayat shows that true faith lies in mercy, balance, and following Allah SWT’s commands—not in man-made extremes or self-imposed hardship. Allah SWT tells us to pray, marry, have children but never ignore deen. DEEN + DUNYA = SUCCESS.
After many messengers, Allah SWT raised ʿĪsā (Jesus), son of Mary, gave him the Injīl (Gospel), and put gentleness and mercy in the hearts of his true followers.
Later these people innovated and invented Monasticism (withdrawing from the world) which was not prescribed by Allah SWT. They claimed it was to please Allah SWT.

Monasticism is a religious way of life where individuals withdraw from worldly pursuits to dedicate themselves to spiritual activities, characterized by seclusion, self-discipline, vows (like poverty, chastity, obedience), and a structured routine of prayer, work, and contemplation, found in traditions like Christianity, Buddhism, and Hinduism.
Brief History:

Early Christians later made celibacy/asceticism an ideal, turning harsh self-denial into a religious goal. At times pushing extremes (severe self-punishment, abandoning family life, treating marriage as impure). This was not sustainable/unnatural way of life and lead to moral abuse, and sectarian fights.
True believers—then and now—are those who follow revelation with sincerity, not human-made extremes.
Allah SWT dislikes innovations in religion and extremes in religion. Balance is a must.

translation.text: O people of faith! Fear Allah and believe in His Messenger. ˹And˺ He will grant you a double share of His mercy, provide you with a light to walk in ˹on Judgment Day˺, and forgive you. For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: Believers (this can mean those who believe in previous scriptures or those who believe in Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) are commanded to have God consciousness or taqwa of Allah SWT and truly believe in His Messenger.

If they do so, Allah SWT will bless them with double mercy — one for accepting faith and another for remaining sincere and steadfast in it. He will also give them a guiding light to help them walk the right path in this world and in the Hereafter, and He will forgive their sins, both from ignorance before faith and from human weakness afterward. Allah is Most Forgiving and Most Merciful.
Lesson: Do the best you can for Allah SWT and Allah will give you more than you ever expect – now and in the Hereafter.

translation.text: ˹This is so˺ that the People of the Book ˹who deny the Prophet˺ may know that they do not have any control over Allah’s grace, and that all grace is in Allah’s Hands. He grants it to whoever He wills. For Allah is the Lord of infinite bounty.

commentary.text: Let not any race, or people, or community, or group, believe that they have exclusive possession of Allah SWT's Grace, or that they can influence its grant or its withholding. Allah's Grace is free, and entirely controlled by Him, independently of any priests and privileged people. He dispenses it according to His own wise and Holy Will and Plan; and to His Grace there is no limit.
Allah SWT is the final JUDGE! He will decide the ultimate fate of every person.
Lesson: Intolerance in faith leads to enmity and division.
Dua. Allah huma Afini in Dunya and Hereafter.

items.text: LIP SERVICE IN NOT ENOUGH RATHER ACTION IS REQUIRED. SPEND IN THE WAY OF ALLAH SWT – SPEND WITH YOUR MONEY, TIME, ENERGY, KNOWLEDGE, AND CORE COMPETENCIES.
(57:7) Believe in Allah and in His Messenger and expend of what He has entrusted to you. A great reward awaits those of you who believe and spend their wealth.

(57:10) And why should you not spend in the cause of Allah, while Allah is the ˹sole˺ inheritor of the heavens and the earth? Those of you who donated and fought before the victory ˹over Mecca˺ are unparalleled. They are far greater in rank than those who donated and fought afterwards. Yet Allah has promised each a fine reward. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
(57:11) Who is it that will give Allah a beautiful loan? A loan that Allah will repay after increasing it many times and grant him a generous reward.
Also see Ayat 18
(57:18) Indeed, those men and women who give in charity and lend to Allah a good loan will have it multiplied for them, and they will have an honourable reward.
Also see Ayat 11

TRAITS ALLAH SWT DOES NOT LIKE: HYPOCRISY, FALSE HOPES OR ASSUMPTIONS, LAMENTING WHAT COULD BE, ARROGANCE, BOASTFULNESS, STINGINESS, ENCOURAGING OTHERS TO BE STINGY, DISBELIEF, TRANGRESSION/REBELLION, INNOVATIONS/INVENTIONS IN RELIGION AND NO EXTREMES, i.e. MONASTICISM.

(57:14) The tormented will cry out to those graced, “Were we not with you?” They will reply, “Yes ˹you were˺. But you chose to be tempted ˹by hypocrisy˺, ˹eagerly˺ awaited ˹our demise˺, doubted ˹the truth˺, and were deluded by false hopes until Allah’s decree ˹of your death˺ came to pass. And ˹so˺ the Chief Deceiver deceived you about Allah.
(57:23) ˹We let you know this˺ so that you neither grieve over what you have missed nor boast over what He has granted you. For Allah does not like whoever is arrogant, boastful—
(57:24) those who are stingy and promote stinginess among people. And whoever turns away ˹should know that˺ Allah ˹alone˺ is truly the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

(57:27) Then in the footsteps of these ˹prophets˺, We sent Our messengers, and ˹after them˺ We sent Jesus, son of Mary, and granted him the Gospel, and instilled compassion and mercy into the hearts of his followers.
